subject: physics
question_text: State Pascal's law. Mention its applications.

mark_split.label: Pressure equal at the same height

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 (Mechanical Properties of Fluids), Short Answer Question 2 (printed p.107). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The four-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: for a fluid at rest the pressure is the same at every point at the same height, and a change of pressure applied at any point of an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every point of the fluid and to the walls of the container; the hydraulic lift, the hydraulic brake and the hydraulic press all work by this law. This card states the law and names the applications; a separate 4-mark question explains how the lift and the brakes work.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Pressure equal at the same height
lines: For a fluid at rest, the
pressure is the same at every
point that is at the same
steps.margin_note: First mark. State that the pressure depends only on height, not on position.
steps.why: This is the first half of Pascal's law, and it is what makes 'the pressure at a height' a meaningful single number.
common_mistakes: Saying the pressure is the same everywhere in the fluid, without the same-height condition.
Confusing this with the second half of the law, about pressure transmitted through the fluid.

recall.must_convey: That in a fluid at rest the pressure is the same at all points at the same height.
accept: at rest, equal pressure at equal height

steps.memory_tip: Same height means same pressure, for a fluid at rest.

steps.label: Pascal's law stated
lines: every point of the fluid and
to the walls of the container.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say 'undiminished' — the change reaches every point at full strength.
steps.why: This is the working part of the law, and it is the reason a small force applied at one point can act as a large force elsewhere, which every application below relies on.
common_mistakes: Saying the pressure is transmitted, without 'undiminished' — the strength does not fall along the way.
Restricting the statement to liquids only, when the law holds for any fluid at rest.

recall.must_convey: That a pressure change applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every point and to the container walls.
accept: pressure change reaches every point equally

steps.memory_tip: Undiminished is the key word — the change reaches every point at full strength.

steps.label: Three applications named
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Name all three devices.
steps.why: Naming the devices is itself the mark here; the working of each is separate ground.
common_mistakes: Naming only one or two of the three devices.
Naming a device that is not built on Pascal's law, such as a barometer.

recall.must_convey: The three named devices: the hydraulic lift, the hydraulic brake and the hydraulic press.

steps.memory_tip: Three hydraulic devices: lift, brake, press — all three from one law.

steps.label: The hydraulic press
steps.mark_note: What the press is used for
lines: The hydraulic press is used to
It works on the same law as
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Give at least one real use of the hydraulic press.
steps.why: Naming a real use shows the application is understood, not just recited from a list of names.
common_mistakes: Describing the press with no example of what it is used for.
Confusing the press with the hydraulic lift — the press compresses or crushes; it does not raise a load.

recall.must_convey: At least one real use of the hydraulic press, such as compressing cotton, crushing scrap metal, or extracting oil from seeds.
reject: raises a load on a large piston

steps.memory_tip: The press compresses and crushes; the lift raises. Different jobs, same law.

insider_note: Four marks, four short facts: two halves of the law, the three names, and one real use of the press. A student who writes only the formula-free statement and no application usually stops at two marks.
